title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two fragments, separated by a horizontal rule. Both belong to the setting of Kummer theory and the tame fundamental group, which matches the folder title 'Théorie de Kum[m]er'.

(1) Top fragment. Fix a geometric point s̄ of a scheme S. Grothendieck writes a homomorphism from the étale fundamental group Π_1(S,s̄) towards the projective limit of the μ_n over S, with n restricted to integers prime to the residue characteristic(s), i.e. invertible on S. This is the cyclotomic character. π_1(S,s̄) acts on the fibres μ_n(s̄) of the finite étale group schemes μ_n. Passing to the limit gives a continuous action on the Tate module Ẑ'(1) = lim μ_n, hence a character π_1(S,s̄) → Aut(Ẑ'(1)) = Ẑ'^×. The second target of the arrow is cut off; most likely it was 'Aut(lim μ_n(s̄))' or the start of a Kummer-type construction. In Kummer theory one attaches to a unit f in Γ(S,O_S^×) the μ_n-torsors given by n-th roots of f. In the limit these yield a homomorphism from π_1 of the cover to lim μ_n, or a class in H^1(S, Ẑ'(1)).

(2) Bottom fragment. K is a henselian discretely valued field with valuation ring V, residue field k of characteristic p, and K̄ an algebraic closure. Grothendieck writes the exact sequence
1 → lim_{(n,p)=1} μ_n(K̄) → π_1(K) → π_1(k) → 1,
together with the identification π_1(k) = π_1(V). The latter holds because V is henselian, so finite étale covers of V correspond to those of k (Hensel's lemma / SGA1).

The kernel is the tame inertia group, identified with Ẑ'(1) = ∏_{l≠p} Z_l(1) by Kummer theory. Since V is henselian, the tamely ramified extensions of K are obtained by adjoining n-th roots, (n,p)=1, of a uniformizer to unramified extensions. Hence the tame inertia is the limit of the μ_n, and the outer action of π_1(k) on it is the cyclotomic character of fragment (1).

The point of the page is the basic structure of the tame fundamental group of a henselian discretely valued field, and its relation to the cyclotomic character, as a starting point for the Kummer-theory notes in this folder.
errors: As written with the full π_1(K), the sequence is not exact on the left when p>0: the kernel of π_1(K) → π_1(k) is the whole inertia group, an extension of Ẑ'(1) by the wild inertia (a pro-p group). The sequence is correct only for the tame quotient π_1^t(K), or for the maximal prime-to-p part of inertia. The mark '+' on the arrow may be a subscript 't' (tame), which would make the statement correct.
Minor: π_1(k) = π_1(V) requires V henselian (e.g. complete). This is implicit in the notation.

Top line: the target of the arrow from Π_1(S,s̄) is incomplete. As a homomorphism to Ẑ'(1) it would only make sense in a Kummer construction attached to a unit or to a cover. The intrinsic object is the cyclotomic character to Aut(Ẑ'(1)) = Ẑ'^×.

ideas.what: Action of π_1(S,s̄) on the Tate module lim μ_n (n invertible on S), i.e. the cyclotomic character / Kummer homomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: cyclotomic character; Kummer map to H^1(S, Ẑ'(1))
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Kummer, Serre, Tate); étale version in SGA1/SGA4
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental group), SGA4 IX/X and SGA 4½ (Kummer theory in étale cohomology)

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → Ẑ'(1) → π_1^tame(K) → π_1(k) → 1 for a henselian discretely valued field, with π_1(k) = π_1(V)
ideas.modern_name: structure of the tame fundamental group / tame inertia ≅ Ẑ'(1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical local class field theory / Abhyankar's lemma; Grothendieck–Murre for the scheme-theoretic tame π_1
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. XIII (Abhyankar's lemma, tame ramification); Grothendieck–Murre, LNM 208 (1971)

deep.surprise_reason: The page records textbook facts: the cyclotomic action on lim μ_n and the tame inertia exact sequence for a henselian discretely valued field. Both are standard and appear in SGA1 and Grothendieck–Murre. There is no new construction or connection.
transcription_corrections: Top left should read 's̄ ∈ S, s̄ pt géométrique' (the geometric point is s̄; S is the base scheme).
'n premier à s' is probably 'n premier à p' or 'n inversible sur S'; the handwriting is ambiguous.
The '+' on the arrow after μ_n(K̄) may be a subscript 't' marking the tame fundamental group π_1^t(K).
Under the second arrow, 'n premier à p' is correctly read.
